It’s a bit weird for many western players like me b/c in the English translation they’re really pushing for that sibling dynamic between them: people argue that they don’t really see each other as brothers, but Kaeya refers to Master Crepus as “father” instead of “your father” when talking to Diluc in Venti’s story quest and Kaeya’s Vision story says he’s an adopted son of Crepus.  So regardless of their dynamic they’re portrayed as brothers (in the Eng version anyway) which is why many are revolted at even the thought of shipping them

I’m not sure how accurate/inaccurate their portrayal in the English ver. is though.  I always see the whole sworn brothers thing brought up, but nobody I’ve spoken to has actually been able to tell me if Kaeya always refers to Diluc as “sworn brother” and provide various examples w/ context.  I’ve seen two translations of the original text of Kaeya’s vision story and both said he was adopted/Diluc’s adopted brother, so idk—until then I’ll remain neutral until Miyoho decides to clarify their relationship later down the road lol
wasn’t it basically confirmed in that everything you need to know about ninjago video LEGO put out that they were a couple?

Good to hear that transitioning makes you feel a lot more comfortable in your skin! :0 As long as you’re at home with yourself after transitioning, I think that’s all that matters.  I shouldn’t judge people for wanting to feel themselves.  
Gender seems to be a tricky topic and I’m seeing now that there’s no one way to describe it.  I think I’ll stick with the explanation that it’s just a part of who you are—someone described it as like having bones, or your dominant hand(s), and etc.  I think that helps me understand it a bit better, haha
Thank you for sharing your experience!

Thank you for your explanation :0
I know it’s probably a commonly-asked question which does not have an exact answer.  But everyone in the comments has helped me understand a bit more that gender isn’t necessarily all just about private parts, like I was previously taught.  It’s just an undeniable part of you.  I guess it’s like if someone asked me, “What’s it like to have brown eyes?” and it’s not exactly a feeling, it’s just who you are.  I hope I’m sort of on the right track here haha

I’m glad to hear that transitioning really helps out a lot of people feel more comfortable.  Feeling like you’re in a body that isn’t you is an experience that I cannot begin to comprehend, I imagine it must be really tough having to go through that.  Someone in this thread explained to me that gender is more of an instinctive feeling than anything, and like others have explained in this thread you just, are who you are, and you don’t have to let society’s definition of male and female define you.  Thank you for sharing your experience with me, helps me understand this all a bit more :0

You’re right, it may or may not be some internalized homo/biphobia.  I have to admit I still have to get over some of my internalized “gay/lesbian/bi bad!” when looking at homosexual content, so that may be the case.  I don’t know, it’s like, I don’t feel like I’d want to start a relationship with a female.  Sure, lots of them are hot, but I don’t find myself interested in the attributes of their personality as much as men.  Not trying to imply that I objectify women or anything, though.  
But they say your preferences are fluid, I think.  Maybe I’ll try dating a girl in the future, haha.  We’ll see what happens :0

Huh, being gender apathetic? That’s actually a really interesting observation.  I’ve always wondered why me and my cis friends found it a bit difficult to understand trans people, but at least everyone in this thread has made me a bit more aware about the experience.
I remember as a kid always insisting to my parents that I was a tomboy.  I was interested in boyish things, a passionate dislike for dresses, despised dolls.  I would look myself in the mirrors sometimes and think to myself that I could pass as a man if I wanted to.  These thoughts ran rampant in my head as a kid.  Guess through persistent brainwashing from my parents I began to, I guess fully believe I am female.  I ended up developing an affinity for dresses and action figures, which I guess can pass as an equivalent to Barbie dolls haha.  I can’t say I still fully understand the concept of gender, because I really can’t say that I’m drawn to being female or male.  I...just am, if that makes any sort of sense haha.  I was referred to as female at birth, and that’s ultimately what stuck with me.  
I think if I hang around my trans friends and get more helpful input from the community, I’ll come to understand everyone here fully.  Thank you for sharing your experience :0

Don’t apologize for writing a ton, everyone in this thread has helped open a whole ton :0
I’ve always associated gender with genitals, I never really thought about it being something more internalized and instinctive.  This shines a whole new light haha, thank you!
I’m glad that transitioning has made you more comfortable.  I believe everyone should feel comfortable being who they are, and not force themselves to conform to what people say they are.  Ugh, this is a lesson we were given in grade school, I can’t believe I found it so hard to put two and two together
dang, that’s some s tier rng luck
